atlas-th.0001: A university study and graduate work destination: the Non-ED Plus visa offers 1-year post-study job search and in-country work transition, alongside Non-B corporate permits and BOI schemes. Bangkok, the capital, is home to the stock exchange.
atlas-th.0002: The capital and home of the stock exchange
atlas-th.0003: Thailand was not covered by the research library before this record.
atlas-th.0004: Thailand visas, student work prohibitions, Non-ED Plus 1-year graduate routes, Non-B work permits (50,000 THB minimum salary) and DTV are fully verified in visas_immigration/thailand/thailand_visas_immigration_guide.md.
atlas-th.0005: No source read gives Bangkok’s jobs by sector: the national planning office’s provincial accounts give output, not jobs, so no family is rated above present.
atlas-th.0006: Pay and tax series by province were not researched: the labour-force survey’s averages are by region, not by province.
atlas-th.0007: The Stock Exchange of Thailand is based in its own building at 93 Ratchadaphisek Road, Din Daeng, Bangkok.
atlas-th.0008: The UK Foreign Office advises against all but essential travel to Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat provinces and four districts of southern Songkhla, near the Malaysian border, because of regular attacks, and to areas within 20 km of the border with Cambodia after fighting in 2025.
atlas-th.0009: The industrial corridor east of Bangkok, now attracting data centres
atlas-th.0012: On 6 May 2026 the Board of Investment approved data-centre projects in the Eastern Economic Corridor, among them Skyline Data Center and Cloud Services in Chachoengsao (46 billion baht, 200 MW of IT load) and Bridge Data Centres in Chonburi (24.6 billion baht, 134 MW).
atlas-th.0013: No family is rated in the Eastern Economic Corridor: the source read lists investment approvals, not hiring.
atlas-th.0014: On 2 October 2026 the Stock Exchange of Thailand showed a market capitalisation of THB 19,831,438.51 million for the SET board and THB 215,537.25 million for the mai board.
atlas-th.0015: The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) ranks Bangkok 88th in the world, up 12 places.
atlas-th.0016: Kasikornbank reports 17,194 employees and 732 domestic branches at the end of 2025.
atlas-th.0017: The national planning office puts Bangkok’s gross provincial product at THB 6,351,792 million in 2024 (provisional), THB 697,529 per person, for a population estimate of 9.1 million.
atlas-th.0018: The national planning office puts Chon Buri’s gross provincial product at THB 1,234,303 million in 2024 (provisional), THB 601,977 per person, for a population estimate of 2.05 million.
atlas-th.0019: No pay figure is given: the labour-force survey’s averages are by region, not by province, so Bangkok and Chonburi could not be compared like with like. Bangkok Bank, Siam Commercial Bank and PTT are not named because no source we can cite was read, and Kasikornbank’s head office is not stated in the summary read.
atlas-th.0020: Ratchadaphisek Road, Bangkok; market capitalisation THB 19.8 trillion
atlas-th.0024: In the 2026 TOEIC survey of Thai HR executives, 97% called English important and 80% used English assessments in recruitment and screening.
atlas-th.0025: There is no single national graduate season: Deloitte’s Amplify internships for May to August 2025 closed on 30 March 2025, KBank’s 2024 Young Scholarship closed on 15 January 2024, and the civil service general-knowledge exam for 2026 took registrations from 14 January to 3 February 2026.
atlas-th.0026: Among company hires recorded by the Board of Investment, the share of university graduates fell from 30.1% in 2018 to 17.2% in 2022 while secondary-school graduates rose from 41.1% to 57.3%; the NESDC report warns that new graduates may struggle to find jobs as demand falls.
atlas-th.0027: Thai graduates enter through job portals (JobThai listed 121,450 jobs the day it was read), structured employer programmes and university co-operative placements; a foreign graduate needs an employer that can sponsor a work permit, which takes THB 2 million of paid-up capital and four Thai employees per foreigner unless the company is Board of Investment-promoted.
atlas-th.0028: In the JobsDB hiring report for 2022-2023, seven in ten large organisations had hired recent graduates and more than half had taken interns. Several universities build a work placement into the degree, and employers say they use it to judge students before hiring.
atlas-th.0029: Co-operative education and internship that turns into an offer
atlas-th.0030: Walailak University runs an eight-month co-operative placement for all its programmes, with more than 2,500 students placed in fiscal year 2026 across more than 2,700 partner organisations; partner executives say the placement lets them assess students before considering them for future employment.
atlas-th.0031: SCB runs a four-month co-operative programme for fourth-year students from leading Thai universities in data analytics and software engineering. No published rate of conversion from internship to offer was found for Thailand.
atlas-th.0032: Central Group’s two-year Management Associate Program asks for a master’s degree in any field, an age of 28 or under and up to 3 years of work experience, and runs seven stages from an online test to an assessment centre.
atlas-th.0033: Deloitte’s Amplify programme offered more than 100 twelve-week internships in Bangkok in 2025 and says interns who do well will be offered full-time jobs; KBank’s Young Scholarship sends scholars to a master’s abroad after three years of work at the bank.
atlas-th.0034: JobThai listed 121,450 jobs on the day it was read, with filters for new graduates, internships, AI jobs and salary bands; JobsDB is the other large board. In the JobsDB report, employers weigh the interview, the attitude to work and the field of study.
atlas-th.0036: JobsDB runs an annual campus programme with more than 20 universities (talks, a résumé clinic), and private fairs such as the WakuWaku Job Fair of 22 February 2025 in Bangkok held on-the-spot interviews for fresh graduates and experienced people.
atlas-th.0037: Recruitment firms and the experienced hire
atlas-th.0038: Recruitment firms such as Personnel Consultant advise checking company career pages regularly and keeping a profile with an uploaded résumé, so that recruiters can find you when suitable roles open. No survey of the share of experienced hires made this way was found, so the ranking is anecdotal.
atlas-th.0039: In mid-2026 university graduates had the highest unemployment rate of any education level, 1.6%, while more than 300,000 vacancies were open: a mismatch more than a shortage. The graduate share of company hires fell from 30.1% in 2018 to 17.2% in 2022.
atlas-th.0040: About 215,000 new bachelor’s graduates were expected to enter the labour market in 2025, and the Ministry of Labour put unemployment among 15-to-24-year-olds at 5.89%, the highest of any age group.
atlas-th.0041: Windows that were published: Deloitte’s May-to-August 2025 internships closed on 30 March 2025, and KBank’s 2024 scholarship closed on 15 January 2024. Central Group’s page gives no window. There is no single national season.
atlas-th.0042: KBank recruits future leaders through its Young Scholarship: five full scholarships in the 2024 round for final-year students with a GPA of at least 3.25, who first work at the bank in wealth, credit or data for three years. SCB lists a special-programme page for new graduates, but its details could not be opened.
atlas-th.0043: A career guide says the ACCA qualification is recognised in Thailand alongside the Thai CPA.
atlas-th.0044: Supervising and auditing accounts is one of the occupations reserved for Thai nationals, so a foreign graduate cannot sign off audits in Thailand.
atlas-th.0045: Retail and consumer groups run trainee tracks of their own: Central Group’s Management Associate Program is a two-year rotation in retail that ends in a leadership role, with an open house and an assessment centre in the selection.
atlas-th.0046: Deloitte’s Amplify internships in Bangkok were open to graduating students from all disciplines and to graduates with under 3 years of experience; no page was read for the strategy firms in Bangkok.
atlas-th.0047: New graduates report gaps in English, digital skills and soft skills; multinationals and Bangkok’s tech firms hire IT graduates, and SCB’s four-month co-operative programme puts fourth-year students on live software and data work.
atlas-th.0048: No source read ranks Thai universities by employer demand. SCB takes co-op students from “leading Thai universities” without naming them, and Walailak places its students through the university itself.
atlas-th.0049: JobsDB’s university activation visits more than 20 universities each year, and private fairs such as the WakuWaku Job Fair (22 February 2025, Grande Centre Point Terminal 21, Bangkok) offer on-the-spot interviews.
atlas-th.0050: Job boards post vacancies all year and carry a “new graduate” filter; the programme windows found (Deloitte, KBank) are short and tied to an intake.
atlas-th.0051: Central Group’s Management Associate Program asks for a master’s degree in any field. The other programmes found do not: Deloitte’s Amplify takes graduating students and graduates with under 3 years of experience, and KBank’s scholarship takes final-year students with a GPA of at least 3.25.
atlas-th.0052: Accounting and auditing, Thai law, architecture and civil engineering are reserved for Thai nationals or Thai-licensed professionals (CPA, architect, engineer licences), with narrow exceptions for specialised expertise.
atlas-th.0053: For a work permit the employer files a copy of your degree, and most jobs expect at least a bachelor’s degree. Until 28 February 2027 an Italian degree needs full consular legalisation, because the Hague Apostille does not yet apply.
